landing_note: Kim et al. 2025, Scientific Reports — a Korean two-cohort GWAS on self-aware sleep duration (n = 8,840) with a Drosophila Wwox loss-of-function follow-up. Newest-first. SLEEP IS A DECLARED AXIS OF THE PROBAND PRIORITY MATRIX, and this is the only paper in the corpus that measures it directly against WWOX.

group_assessment.weighting: The cohort is real and well-characterised and the fly experiment is competently run with an adequate n and a backcrossed background. What the paper cannot bear is the weight its title and abstract place on it, and the authors say so themselves in the limitations — which is why every entry below is anchored on their own statements rather than on an external standard.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE HUMAN ASSOCIATION DOES NOT REACH GENOME-WIDE SIGNIFICANCE, AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO IN THEIR OWN LIMITATIONS. The conventional threshold is 5 × 10⁻⁸; Table 2 gives 1.11 × 10⁻⁷ and 2.05 × 10⁻⁷ for the two lead SNVs — two to four times above it. The abstract reports both p-values without qualification and the title of the paper asserts the association. This is not concealed, it is placed where fewest readers go.
entries.snippet: the WWOX gene did not reach the conventional genome-wide significance level in the human GWAS results
entries.found_or_sought: sought — a GWAS claim is a threshold claim, so the first thing to check is which side of the threshold it is on

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND THE EFFECT IS ABOUT A QUARTER OF AN HOUR, WHICH NO SENTENCE IN THE PAPER STATES IN MINUTES. Table 3's betas are in HOURS: for minor homozygotes, −0.209 h at rs16948804 and −0.304 h at rs4887991. That is TWELVE AND EIGHTEEN MINUTES of sleep, against a cohort standard deviation of 1.4 hours — roughly 0.15 to 0.22 SD. INFERENZA with a direct bearing on this corpus: an intronic common-variant effect of a quarter-hour in middle-aged adults is a different biological object from biallelic WWOX loss of function, and nothing licenses reading one as evidence about the other. The unit is what hides it — hours make 0.3 look substantial where minutes would not.
entries.anchor: Table 3, self-aware sleep duration row for rs16948804, heterozygous and minor-homozygous columns
entries.found_or_sought: sought — converted the paper's own betas into the unit a reader thinks in, which is the cheapest audit in a genetics paper

entries.proposition: AND THE SECOND STATED LIMITATION IS THE ONE THAT EXPLAINS THE FIRST. Two cohorts of 4,635 and 4,205 are small for a quantitative-trait GWAS, and the authors name it. Recorded beside entries[0] because together they say what the paper is: an underpowered discovery that did not clear threshold, followed by a functional experiment offered in place of the power.
entries.snippet: the number of subjects in each cohort was not sufficient for GWAS
entries.anchor: Discussion, limitations paragraph, immediately following entries[0]

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND THE PHENOTYPE IS A QUESTIONNAIRE, WITH A DERIVED VARIABLE THAT CANNOT MEAN WHAT IT SAYS. Sleep duration is self-reported for the past month, at a baseline collected 2001-2003. From it the study derives habitual sleep efficiency as duration divided by time in bed, and Table 1 reports it as 98.3 ± 12.6%. A MEAN OF 98.3% WITH AN SD OF 12.6 ON A QUANTITY BOUNDED AT 100% REQUIRES A LARGE FRACTION OF VALUES ABOVE 100% — participants reporting more sleep than time in bed. Measured sleep efficiency by actigraphy or polysomnography in this age range is typically 85-90%. The variable is not used for the paper's main claim, and Table 3 correctly reports no association with it; recorded because a corpus that later reached for 'sleep efficiency' from this cohort would be reaching for an artefact of self-report arithmetic.
entries.found_or_sought: sought — asked what the phenotype physically is, and the derived variable answered louder than the primary one

entries.proposition: THE FLY RESULT, AND IT SPLITS BY TIME OF DAY RATHER THAN REPRODUCING THE HUMAN DIRECTION. Daytime sleep falls, night-time sleep rises. The abstract states both, honestly. What 'confirmatory experiments' and 'confirmed the functional relevance' cannot mean is that the fly reproduced the human phenotype: the human finding is a reduction in total self-reported duration, and the fly gives a redistribution across the light cycle whose net is a modest reduction.
entries.snippet: In Wwoxf04545 flies, daytime sleep was reduced throughout the day (p-value < 0.0001), whereas night-time sleep was higher and lasted longer than that in control flies
entries.anchor: Results, Drosophila section, describing Figure 2B and 2C

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND THE FIGURE'S OWN TITLE CLAIMS MORE THAN ITS PANEL D SUPPORTS. Figure 2 is titled 'Deletion of Wwox changed sleep duration WITHOUT AFFECTING THE CIRCADIAN RHYTHM', and the evidence offered for the second half is panel E: free-running period and rhythmicity are equivalent, 23.5 h and 96.9% against 96.7%. But panel D shows the mutant's EVENING ACTIVITY PEAK MARKEDLY BLUNTED — the control rises to roughly 100 beam counts per 30 min at ZT11-12 where the mutant reaches about 60 — while the morning peak is far more similar. In Drosophila that evening rise is anticipatory behaviour driven by the clock's evening oscillator, and IT CAN BE LOST WITH AN INTACT FREE-RUNNING PERIOD: period measures the pacemaker, anticipation measures its coupling to behaviour. INFERENZA: 'without affecting the circadian rhythm' is supported for the pacemaker and not for its output, and the two are different claims wearing one phrase. Panel B agrees — the night-time gain is not uniform but concentrated in the late night, where controls become active and mutants do not.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2, panels B, D and E. B: sleep profile in 30-minute bins across ZT0-24, grey w1118 and olive Wwox-f04545, dark phase shaded from ZT12; the grey trace shows a daytime siesta peak near 30 min per bin around ZT5-8 that the olive trace does not reach, and in the shaded night both traces sit near 30 min per bin until roughly ZT20 after which the GREY trace declines toward 20-25 while the olive stays at ceiling. D: activity in beam counts per 30 min on the same axis; both genotypes show a morning peak near ZT0-1 of roughly 110 and 95 counts, and an evening peak at ZT11-12 where GREY reaches about 100 and OLIVE only about 60. E: free-running period bars, both at approximately 23.5 h, with rhythmicity printed inside the bars as 96.9% and 96.7%.
entries.anchor: Figure 2 panels B, D and E
entries.qualifies_needle: The alteration of sleep duration could not be attributed to a defective core circadian clock
entries.found_or_sought: sought — a figure title containing the word 'without' is a negative claim, and negatives are what this corpus checks first

entries.proposition: THE TEXT'S CIRCADIAN CLAIM, RECORDED AS THE TARGET OF THE PANEL ABOVE. Its evidence is the free-running period and rhythmicity, correctly cited.
entries.snippet: The alteration of sleep duration could not be attributed to a defective core circadian clock, as the free-running periods and rhythmicity were equivalent

entries.proposition: A CHECK THAT CAME BACK NEGATIVE FOR THE PAPER, RECORDED BECAUSE A SCREEN THAT ONLY REPORTS HITS IS NOT A SCREEN. Reduced activity WITH reduced daytime sleep looked incoherent to me — in Drosophila sleep is defined as five minutes without beam crossings, so less activity ought to mean more scored sleep. The authors use it to argue the sleep phenotype is not a locomotion artefact, and they are right: the resolution is fragmentation, which panel F confirms by showing daytime average bout length reduced. Short, broken activity prevents five-minute quiescent windows without raising total beam counts. The data are coherent and my objection was wrong.
entries.snippet: Wwoxf04545 fly activity was lower throughout the day, which implied that the sleep phenotype of Wwoxf04545 did not simply result from reduced locomotor activity
entries.found_or_sought: sought — went to check an apparent incoherence and found the paper had already resolved it

entries.proposition: AND THE SAME PARTNER LIST APPEARS A FOURTH TIME TODAY. The Discussion's one-sentence account of WWOX function names p73, ErbB4, Ap2γ, RUNX2 and HIF1α as WW-domain partners. Those are the partners of PMID 16061658 page-adjudicated this morning (ErbB4, p73, AP-2γ) and PMID 18487609 read this morning (RUNX2), and three of them turned up in the neural-progenitor leading edge of PMID 31543760 an hour ago. Recorded not as a finding of this paper — it is a review sentence with citations — but because FOUR INDEPENDENT PAPERS READ IN ONE DAY CONVERGE ON ONE PARTNER SET, and that convergence is the argument for treating the WW/PPxY competition network as the corpus's central mechanistic object rather than as an oncology detail.
